hero.title: Transfer files from PC to phone
hero.body: No cable, no emailing a file to yourself. BIShare moves files from any Windows, Mac, or Linux computer straight onto your iPhone or Android — over your local Wi-Fi, or with a link your phone opens in any browser. No cloud upload, no account.

why.title: The cable-and-inbox problem
why.body: Getting a file from your computer onto your phone usually means digging out the right cable and hoping the drivers cooperate — or emailing it to yourself and fighting the attachment size limit. Neither is quick, and neither plays nice across brands. BIShare skips both: your files go straight from computer to phone, wirelessly, with nothing parked on a server.

how.title: Two ways to land a file on your phone

0.b: Your computer and phone find each other on the local network and send directly, end-to-end encrypted — nothing touches a server. It's quick, and it still works on a phone hotspot with no internet at all.

1.b: You get a link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. Open the link in any phone browser and download — no app, no sign-up. The link expires on its own after 24 hours.

2.b: Windows, Mac, and Linux to iPhone or Android — one app, both directions. Push files onto your phone, or pull them back to your PC.

0.q: How do I transfer files from PC to phone without a cable?
0.a: Install BIShare on your computer and your phone. On the same Wi-Fi, pick the phone and send — files go directly, end-to-end encrypted, with no server in the middle. Not on the same network? Share the link or QR code and open it in your phone's browser to download.

1.q: How do I move files from my computer to my iPhone?
1.a: With BIShare the iPhone needs no Lightning cable, no iTunes, no Finder. Send from the computer over Wi-Fi and accept on the iPhone, or open the share link in Safari and tap download. Photos, videos, PDFs — any file type works.

2.q: Can I send large files from PC to phone?
2.a: Yes. Nearby transfers over your own Wi-Fi have no size limit at all. Share links carry files up to 100 GB for free — far past any email attachment cap.

3.q: Do I need to install an app on the phone?
3.a: Not to receive a browser link — just open it and download, no app and no account. Installing BIShare on the phone makes nearby transfers faster and lets you send files back to the PC, but it's never required to receive.

4.q: Is it safe to transfer files this way?
4.a: Yes. Nearby transfers are end-to-end encrypted and never leave your local network. Share links are encrypted in transit and expire automatically after 24 hours, so nothing lingers online.

cta.title: Get files onto your phone in seconds
cta.body: Free, no account. Install BIShare on your PC, Mac, or Linux and send to any phone — the browser link means the phone doesn't even need the app.
